sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how the two interpretations of "Shuva Yisrael ad" correspond to two levels of light revealed through teshuvah.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain the connection between the two interpretations of "Shuva Yisrael ad" —
(whether this "ad" means "up to and including,"
or whether this "ad" means "up to but not including") —
with the two interpretations of "Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha":

[the interpretation] that Hashem will be your G-d, your strength and vitality, and [the interpretation] that Hashem will be only a level of Elokim and contraction relative to the Ein Sof that is above Hashem.
For the interpretation of "Shuva Yisrael ad" that it is "ad" meaning "up to and including,"
the light to which negative knowledge applies,
which generally is the Or HaSovev (Encompassing Light),
corresponds to the interpretation that "Hashem will be your G-d, your strength and vitality,"
[meaning] the light that is revealed through teshuvah is the Or HaSovev
(Hashem).
And the interpretation of "Shuva Yisrael ad" that it is "ad" meaning "up to but not including,"
the light to which even negative knowledge does not apply,
corresponds to the interpretation that "Hashem will be only a level of Elokim and contraction relative to the Ein Sof that is above Hashem,"
[meaning] the light that is revealed through teshuvah is the light that is above even the Or HaSovev.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the addition of "Hashem Elokecha" after "ad" points to a level higher than even "ad lo biChlal," as even the name Hashem (vocalized as Elokim) is merely a name relative to the Essence.

translations.translation: And on a deeper level, it can be said
that the reason the verse adds "Hashem Elokecha" after already saying "Shuva Yisrael ad,"
is that the concept of "Hashem Elokecha" —
that Hashem is only a level of Elokim and contraction relative to the Ein Sof that is above Hashem —
is higher even than "ad lo biChlal."
And this will be understood based on what was explained above15
that in the word "Hashem" in the verse "Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha," there is also included "Hashem" vocalized as "Elokim,"
which is an exceedingly lofty level,
as explained in Likkutei Torah16
(on the verse17
"Ken Adonai Hashem Yatzmiach Tzedakah...")
the greatness of the elevation of the two names Adonai and Hashem
(vocalized as Elokim).
And nevertheless it is written "ad Hashem Elokecha,"
that even this Hashem is only a level of Elokim and contraction relative to the Ein Sof that is above Hashem,
because even Hashem
(vocalized as Elokim)
is only a name.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah18
regarding the two levels of the shofar that will be in the future,
"And Adonai Hashem will blow the shofar... and He will blow a great shofar,"19
[explaining] that the shofar of "And Adonai Hashem will blow the shofar,"
since even Adonai Hashem
(vocalized as Elokim)
are only names,
is a plain shofar,
but regarding the great shofar it is written "He will blow a great shofar,"
"He will blow" is stated plainly, and it does not say who is the blower,
because this blowing is an efflux and revelation from the aspect of the Hidden of All Hidden.
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah there,
that correspondingly is the difference between Rosh HaShanah and Yom HaKippurim,
that the shofar of Rosh HaShanah is like "And Adonai Hashem will blow the shofar,"
and on Yom HaKippurim it is written20
"Before Hashem you shall be purified,"
above Hashem,21
and moreover,22
"For on this day He will atone for you,"20
"He will atone" is stated plainly, and it does not say who is the atoner,21
like "He will blow a great shofar,"
"He will blow" is stated plainly.
And this is what is said in the haftarah of Shabbos Shuvah,
"Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha,"
that this "Hashem" also refers to Hashem vocalized as Elokim,
because on Shabbos Shuvah there already exists a taste of the elevation of Yom HaKippurim,23
and relative to this elevation, even Hashem vocalized as Elokim is only a level of Elokim and contraction.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that after "ad" (including "ad lo biChlal"), the addition of "Hashem Elokecha" points to the essential connection of the soul with Atzmus, where defect is inherently inapplicable.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain that after the verse says "Shuva Yisrael ad,"
in which is included even "ad lo biChlal,"
it adds "Hashem Elokecha,"
because even the concept of "ad lo biChlal,"
although even negative knowledge does not apply to it
(as above, section 3),
nevertheless, from the fact that it is necessary to negate and say "ad lo biChlal,"
it is understood24
that it has some connection.
And this is like the concept of the Baal HaRatzon (Master of Will) from whom forgiveness is drawn
(as explained above25),
which generally is the concept of the names Adonai and Hashem vocalized as Elokim, through which all defects are filled,26
for although the fact that forgiveness is drawn from Him for that which they did contrary to the will is because He is not compelled in the will,27
nevertheless, the will has a connection to it
(as is proven from the fact that He is called "Baal HaRatzon"),
and therefore the forgiveness must be for that which they did contrary to the will.28
But regarding the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above even the Baal HaRatzon,
defect is inherently inapplicable.
And as explained elsewhere29
regarding the concept that "the essence of the day atones,"30
that the atonement that comes from the essence of the day is
(not in a manner of action,
but rather)
that on this day the connection of the essence of the soul with Atzmus is revealed
(which is above even the Baal HaRatzon),
[such that] relative to this level, defect is inherently inapplicable.
And this is that after it says "Shuva Yisrael ad," it adds "Hashem Elokecha,"
for since Shabbos Shuvah is a preparation for Yom HaKippurim,
therefore the teshuvah of Shabbos Shuvah must be not only "ad,"
[even] "ad lo biChlal,"
through which all defects will be nullified,
but rather it is also necessary to arouse and reveal the point of Yiddishkeit,
the connection of the essence of the soul with Atzmus
(which is above even the Baal HaRatzon),
relative to which even Hashem vocalized as Elokim is only a level of Elokim and contraction,
and through this it is revealed that the undesirable matters are only in externality,
but in internality31
(from the perspective of the connection of Yisrael and the Holy One, Blessed be He),
there were inherently no undesirable things.
